table.name: battle
table.purpose: Battles between the Bulgarian Empire and the Latin Empire (Fourth Crusade / Latin Romania era, c. 1205–1235), listing commanders on each side and the outcome. One row per battle or siege.

bulgarian_commander.name: bulgarian_commander
bulgarian_commander.description: Name of the commander of the Bulgarian forces in the battle; 'Unknown' when not recorded.

date.name: date
date.description: Date of the battle, stored as free text with inconsistent precision (full day, month+year, or year only), e.g. '14 April 1205', 'June 1205', '1235'.

id.name: id
id.description: Primary key of the battle table; unique integer identifier for each battle.

latin_commander.name: latin_commander
latin_commander.description: Name of the commander of the Latin (Crusader/Latin Empire) forces; 'Unknown' when not recorded.

name.name: name
name.description: Name of the battle or siege, e.g. 'Battle of Adrianople', 'Siege of Constantinople'.

result.name: result
result.description: Outcome of the battle: 'Bulgarian victory', 'Latin victory', or 'Two Year Truce'.

table.name: death
table.purpose: Casualty counts (killed/injured) per incident, with a location note naming districts in central/eastern India (Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Bihar, Odisha). The rows most plausibly describe individual violent incidents (e.g. Naxalite/insurgency-related attacks) in India, not the medieval battles or ships elsewhere in this database. The column name 'caused_by_ship_id' and its joins to ship/battle are statistically accepted but semantically inconsistent with the Indian location notes, so its true meaning is unresolved.

id.name: id
id.description: Primary key of the death table; unique integer identifier for each incident row.

injured.name: injured
injured.description: Number of people injured in the incident; 0 in 11 of 13 rows, max 9.

killed.name: killed
killed.description: Number of people killed in the incident; ranges 0–29.

note.name: location
note.description: Location of the incident as 'district, state' in India (e.g. 'Dantewada, Chhattisgarh', 'Bokaro, Jharkhand'). The column is named 'note' but its values are consistently locations.

table.name: ship
table.purpose: Ships (mostly brigs, several Royal Navy) and how they were lost — captured, wrecked, scuttled or sunk — with locations in the English Channel, Mid-Atlantic and SW Approaches. One row per ship. The 'lost_in_battle' column points at battle ids, but those battles are medieval Bulgarian/Latin battles, so the reference is semantically inconsistent and its meaning is unresolved.

disposition_of_ship.name: disposition_of_ship
disposition_of_ship.description: How the ship was lost: 'Captured' (most common), 'Sank', 'Scuttled', or 'Wrecked'.

id.name: id
id.description: Primary key of the ship table; unique integer identifier for each ship.

location.name: location
location.description: Sea area where the ship was lost: 'English Channel', 'Mid-Atlantic', or 'SW Approaches'.

name.name: name
name.description: Name of the ship, e.g. 'HMS Avon', 'Lettice', 'Bacchus'.

ship_type.name: ship_type
ship_type.description: Rig/type of the vessel, mostly 'Brig', with gun counts in some rows ('18-gun Brig', '8 gun Brig').

tonnage.name: tonnage
tonnage.description: Tonnage of the ship as text; numeric where known ('225', '391') and the literal 't' (apparently a placeholder/unknown marker) in 5 of 7 rows.
